passage:
Rajni: Meera hasn't answered in five months. not one reply
Vishal: I know. Have you thought about why?
Rajni: I keep going back to the day I told my daughter in front of everyone that marrying him was a mistake. And the times I read her diary. I never said sorry
Vishal: Will you write to her?
Rajni: One letter. Only an apology. I won't ask her to come home. And I won't call her friends or the aunts any more. I did last year and I think it pushed her further
Vishal: That sounds right. Will you explain yourself in it?
Rajni: No. She decides what happens next
Vishal: I'll sit with you when you write it
Rajni: Thank you. It hurts. But I'd rather she comes back slowly than never

qa.q: How long has Meera not replied?
qa.a: Meera has not replied for five months.

qa.q: What does Rajni feel about the public remark and the diary?
qa.a: Rajni feels regret and sees these as hurtful acts, for which Rajni never apologised.

qa.q: What is Rajni's plan for the letter?
qa.a: One letter with only an apology, without asking Meera to come home and without explaining or defending.

qa.q: How might Meera have felt about the earlier calls to her friends and the aunts?
qa.a: Pressured and pushed further away, as Rajni suspects.

grounding: A parent whose child has cut contact feels hurt, plans an apology without defending, stops pressuring through relatives, and lets the child decide.
